name: Delaware

jury_list.statute: 10 Del. C. 4513(b): 'Records used in the selection process shall not be disclosed, except in accordance with the jury selection plan or as necessary in the preparation or presentation of a motion challenging compliance with this chapter.' Qualification form contents go to the parties in a case (4513(a)).

sources.cite: 10 Del. C. 4509 (non-citizens disqualified; court decides from the qualification form)

voter_file.who_may_get: Anyone may inspect registration records during business hours and make copies (15 Del. C. 1305(a)).

private_challenge.who: No direct private challenge was found. The State Board of Elections may consider removal of names where there is valid reason to believe a person is not qualified, after notice and a hearing (15 Del. C. 1702). 'Any person interested' may appeal to the court from a decision removing or refusing to remove names (15 Del. C. 2101).
private_challenge.form_or_statute: 15 Del. C. 1702, 2101. Not supported by JuryRoll.

county_board.name: Delaware Department of Elections - county office locations

gates.basis: Jury selection records may not be disclosed (10 Del. C. 4513(b)). No direct private challenge found. Strict gates: counts only.

notes: Inspection files exclude Social Security number, date of birth, driver's license number, and phone number (15 Del. C. 1305(a)), so dob_in_public_file is false.
15 Del. C. 1302(c): a registered person who says on a form that they are not a citizen gets 15 days to affirm citizenship in writing or is canceled.
official_pipeline is null: 15 Del. C. 1703 covers felony convictions only. The Superior Court's public jury FAQ asks non-citizens to notify election officials, but no statute requires it.
